newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on primary hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes down on primary hopes.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 50 basis points to 29.50 on Friday after what traders said was a calm session on expectations that primary rates would fall at next week's auction, traders said.
"There's a lot of paper, but not much money. Primary rates are expected to fall next week, so traders are interested in short-term paper only. We'll wait and see," said a trader.
Other traders noted some dealers had pushed rates up on pre-weekend speculation to a midsession high of 30.20 percent.
"There's three days' interest to be taken advantage of, so some dealers force rates up," said a trader.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed flat at 31.50 percent, but had been pushed up to a high of 32 percent by pre-weekend speculation.
Banco de Mexico injected 6.821 billion pesos into the market by auctioning five credits, which it assigned at between 31.57 percent and 32.38 percent.
Traders had originally estimated a liquidity shortfall for the session of 8.866 billion pesos, but said this had been offset by 2.50 billion pesos.
Total credit maturities for Monday were estimated at 4.867 billion pesos.
